newsitem.title: LEBANON: Arab bankers urge governments to reform economies.
newsitem.headline: Arab bankers urge governments to reform economies.

text.p: Arab bankers and financiers meeting in Beirut on Tuesday called on Arab countries to further liberalise their economies to get them ready for the competition they will face when peace comes to the Middle East.

The delegates at the "Arab Banks and Economic Reform Conference" said that according to the latest IMF report the Arab World could become the next big emerging market if their wave of reform continues and if peace prevails in the region.

"...The move towards a solution of the Arab-Israeli crisis and the adoption of economic reform policies in many Middle East states forecast big potential for a better future for Middle Eastern countries in general and Arab countries in particular," Mahmoud Abdul Aziz, head of the Union of Arab Banks, said.

"But this wide potential...will not turn into real chances for gain unless the Arab countries get ready and seriously rehabilitate their economies to become effective regionally and internationally," he told the 240 delegates.

Joseph Tarabey, President of Credit Libanais, one of Beirut's main commerical banks, said the growth rates of Arab economies will rise if they continue to adopt economic reform policies that have borne fruit in other areas in the world.

"The more investment in infrastructure is increased the more the chances for growth strengthen, and in turn the presence of improved infrastructure will attract more investment," added Tarabey, who is also the union's vice-president.

Abdul Aziz said the union has adopted the idea of starting an Arab GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) -- a call he said was backed by the last Arab summit in Cairo earlier this year which called for setting up a main Arab free trade zone.

Citing reforms needed in the Arab banking sector, he said banks need to consolidate their competitive ability by following the world example of establishing giant banking units and should catch up with the information and communications revolution.

Arab banks should also "adopt the concept of universal banking which provides complementary commercial and investment banking services necessary to fund and boost the branches of economic activity in our Arab region," he added.

The Union of Arab Banks sponsoring the two-day meeting said in a study that a number of Arab banks last year set up financial leasing companies, investment banks and companies, merchant banks, brokerage firms and mutual invesment funds.

The study said some Arab banks, in line with the wishes of monetary authorities to develop Arab capital markets, issued new instruments like Global Depository Receipts, hybrid securities and eurobonds in 1995 and some began using derivatives.
"Our region is passing through something like a hard labor and is heading to important and grave changes on all levels, especially the economic level," Tarabey told the meeting.

"No doubt you observe and follow up the preparations that are taking place and projects and orientations being set up, which dictate deep and essential changes take place in the structure and orientation of the Arab economies," he added.
